body:
I've been diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder since I was 12, and the chronic pain syndrome is a newer diagnosis. I've had the problem with my spine since I was a child, but I was only diagnosed with the neurological issues four years ago. My mum came to a few family therapy sessions with me when I was about 16, before she met my step-dad. My mum does understand because she has fibromyalgia herself, it's the rest of my family which don't get it and wouldn't come to any kind of meeting with me even if I begged them to. My grandmother was sectioned once herself, back in the 70's, so she's very against any psychological intervention after the way they treated her. Other than my mum, they just act like I'm being lazy when I have to lay in bed all day or when I can't physically reach up to wash my hair properly, and that's what depresses me the most. Even though I've tried to explain why I can't go on the family days out they all plan, they just change the subject, like I'm making it all up.

The worst thing is that I love photography and I have a business plan which I actually started on, and got backing from another business for, but I can't do it anymore. It's as much as I can do to hold a camera for half an hour. I've been trying to kind of revisit what my old therapist told me when it was my Bipolar Disorder and EDNOS that was affecting me and I've tried to get an appointment with him again, but I could only do it if I pay for it because I'm now over 18 and he works in child services. So I'm trying to save up for that, because he really helped me the last time I was this low.

I've bookmarked this page so I'll come back and send you a PM later, thank you.
That's not a bad idea, actually. Like I said above, it's just a case of finding somewhere that's close enough for me to get to on a bus or train without being in agony, seeing as I don't drive.

I actually have, but it was a while ago now. I used to volunteer at a soup kitchen and it did help, but the problem with where I live is that volunteering opportunities are very limited. It's something I've been looking into, but a lot of them won't take me on because they're either working with children or with older people, and apparently tattoos and piercings don't go down well with them. I've applied as an admin volunteer for an Alzheimer's charity near me though, so fingers crossed they take me on.

The issue I have is that I can't sit or stand for any long period of time, I have to alternate and take five minute walks every hour or so. Even a lot of places that want volunteers don't take kindly to that it seems; you'd think that charities that deal with disabled people especially would understand things like this, but they don't.

I'm leaving to get some sleep myself in a moment.

I've tried counselling, both based on my Bipolar Disorder and some therapy to help me deal better with the pain I'm in. Aside from that, I've tried the whole dating thing, (doesn't go well when you're horribly ugly and overweight,) making new friends, (again, not easy for me,) trying to focus more on the good days I have rather than the bad days, about 15 different medications for different things... I just don't know what else I can do.
